title: Business Licensing and Operational Compliance
summary: This thread tracks the evolution of business eligibility and operational reporting requirements for customs-related activities. It shows a shift from simple import permissions to complex, compliance-heavy requirements involving VAT, industrial status, and mandatory reporting of ownership changes.

evolution.eligibility: Increased from basic registration to specific industrial and tax-compliant status.
evolution.reporting_obligations: Shifted from static licensing to dynamic reporting of internal corporate changes.

timeline.change: Initial restriction on import quantities for commercial business entities.
Introduction of strict eligibility criteria (Industrial IRC holder and VAT compliance) for specific business sectors.
Expansion of business classifications to include specific service providers like express services and e-commerce entities.
Mandatory reporting of ownership or management changes to licensing authorities within a fixed timeframe.

National Board of Revenue: The National Board of Revenue is authorized to specify the quantity of goods that an eligible applicant hotel may import for commercial use.
Commercial Hotel Importation: Applicant hotels are permitted to make a one-time import of goods for commercial operations, provided the quantities are specified by the National Board of Revenue prior to the commencement of business.

(১) (ক) আমদানিকারক প্রতিষ্ঠানকে অবশ্যই Industrial IRC holder VAT compliant Automated Teller Machine (ATM) এবং Closed Circuit Camera উৎপাদনকারী (Manufacturer) হইতে হইবে।
ব্যাখ্যা-
(অ) “Industrial IRC holder” অর্থ এইরূপ প্রতিষ্ঠান যাহার নিকট আমদানি ও রপ্তানি প্রধান নিয়ন্ত্রকের দপ্তর হইতে ইস্যুকৃত হালনাগাদ শিল্প ভোক্তা (Industrial Consumer) আইআরসি রহিয়াছে;
(আ) “VAT compliant” অর্থ মূল্য সংযোজন কর ও সম্পূরক শুল্ক আইন, ২০১২ এর অধীন নিবন্ধিত নিয়মিত দাখিলপত্র (রিটার্ন) দাখিল করে এইরূপ উৎপাদনকারী প্রতিষ্ঠান।

Industrial IRC Holder: This entity refers to an industrial establishment that holds a valid and up-to-date Industrial Import Registration Certificate issued by the Office of the Chief Controller of Imports and Exports.
To qualify as a manufacturer of automated teller machines and closed-circuit cameras, a business must maintain this specific import authorization.
VAT Compliant: A business is considered VAT compliant if it is registered under the Value Added Tax and Supplementary Duty Act, 2012, and regularly submits its required tax returns.
Manufacturing eligibility for certain industrial products is conditional upon maintaining this compliance status.
Manufacturer: This entity refers to an enterprise engaged in the production of specific goods, namely automated teller machines and closed-circuit camera systems.
Manufacturers must satisfy both industrial import registration requirements and tax compliance standards to qualify under this provision.

Industrial IRC Holder: Office of the Chief Controller of Imports and Exports
VAT Compliant: Value Added Tax and Supplementary Duty Act, 2012

On-board Express Service: An On-board Express Service is defined as a person or entity licensed under sub-rule (3) of rule 6 to provide express delivery services for goods through authorized land customs routes.
International Air Express Service: An International Air Express Service refers to a person or entity licensed under sub-rule (3) of rule 6 to provide express delivery services through customs airports.
Cross-Border E-commerce Institution: A cross-border e-commerce institution is defined as a business that displays goods via electronic means, receives orders, and supplies or delivers those goods directly to consumers across international borders using express services.
Gift Goods: Gift goods are defined in accordance with the specific criteria for genuine gift items as described in the Import Policy Order current at the time.
Express Service Provider: This term refers collectively to entities operating as either an On-board Express Service or an International Air Express Service.
Agent: An agent refers to a person or entity that holds a valid license granted under section 243 of the Customs Act.
Customs Computerised Entry Processing Sy: This term is defined by reference to the specific definition provided in section 2, clause (15) of the Customs Act.
Consignee: A consignee is identified as the recipient of goods as specified in the bill of lading, house airway bill, or consignment note issued by the Consignor, principal, or their authorized agent.
Documents: Documents encompass items with no commercial value such as printed materials, technical designs, surveys, catalogs, manuals, passports, and similar items packed in envelopes, cartons, or bundles.
De Minimis: De minimis is defined as per the criteria established in clause (a) of rule 2 of the Customs (De Minimis) Rules, 2019.
Samples: Samples are defined in accordance with the specifications provided for genuine trade samples in the relevant Import Policy Order.
Consignor: The Consignor is defined as the party listed as the sender on the bill of lading, house airway bill, or consignment note, including the principal or their authorized agent.
Forms: This term refers to the specific documents and forms prescribed for use under these rules.
Advertising Materials: Advertising material refers to items defined as genuine advertising goods according to the relevant Import Policy Order.
Person: The term person extends to include companies, partnerships, limited companies, and other legal entities.
Licensee: A license is defined as the authorization granted under rule 6 for the management and customs clearance of goods imported or exported through express service providers.
Licensing Authority: The Licensing Authority refers to the body designated with regulatory powers as described in rule 4.

Warehouse License: The regulations require license holders to notify the licensing authority of any significant changes in the management or ownership structure of their business.
An application for updating these changes must be submitted on the official letterhead of the business within a specific timeframe following approval by the relevant regulatory bodies.
Licensing Authority: The licensing authority is responsible for receiving official applications regarding changes in business ownership or management for entities operating under a warehouse license.
Schedule-3: This schedule specifies the required documentation that must be submitted to the licensing authority when notifying changes in the management or ownership of a licensed warehouse business.
